**Key visual observations:**
- Soybean leaf upper surface with irregularly shaped lesions distributed between the veins
- Lesions show yellow-to-orange chlorotic halos surrounding dark brown/necrotic centers
- Major veins and midrib appear to remain green
- One area of dead tissue has fallen out (ragged hole at leaf margin)
- Lesions are interveinal in distribution

**Reasoning:**
The combination of interveinal chlorotic blotches (yellow spots between veins) with dark necrotic centers, while major veins remain green, is the hallmark pattern of Sudden Death Syndrome (SDS). The SDS description states: "scattered yellow spots between leaf veins that grow into large chlorotic and necrotic blotches between the leaf veins, while the midvein and major lateral veins remain green." This matches closely.

Septoria brown spot produces smaller, uniformly dark brown lesions without the prominent yellow interveinal halos. Bacterial blight tends to produce angular, vein-limited lesions with water-soaking. Soybean Vein Necrosis shows lesions running along veins with vein discoloration, not interveinal blotches.
